data.title: Intel landing Microsoft for EMIB is a 'positive,' but level of importance is unclear: Wedbush
data.description:
The fact that Intel (INTC) landed Microsoft (MSFT) for its advanced packaging technology is a “positive step,” but how financially important it will be is unclear, Wedbush Securities analyst Matt Bryson said.

“Having said this, it's clear Intel has several large EMIB deals,” Bryson wrote in a note to clients. “The question rather in our view is how Intel's packaging efforts ramp amidst ABF constraints.”

The deal will see Microsoft become the first company to use Intel Foundry's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge, or EMIB, advanced packaging technology for Azure first-party silicon. It will also see Intel Xeon CPUs be used in the next-generation server, codenamed Diamond Rapids, and expand the collaboration across Microsoft's Azure roadmap and Intel-based Azure hardware systems.

Separately, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said that the company has signed its first external 18A customer (unnamed and later clarified to be 18AP). Bryson said the deal “had been expected” and is a “positive step forward” for the semiconductor giant. However, the size of the deal and the products involved will determine how meaningful it actually is.

“While this result has been expected, we still see the news as a positive step forward for Intel (though the size of the deal and the products involved will define how meaningful the win is in validating Intel's improvement with its foundry technology),” Bryson added.

data.title: PayPal makes key leadership changes, including a new CFO; former Goldman exec joins board
data.description:
PayPal Holdings (PYPL) named a new chief financial officer on Friday as the company unveiled several leadership changes meant to establish clear strategies across the company's core businesses, simplify its operating model, and align accountability with the company's long-term priorities.

Clare Bramley will become executive vice president and chief financial officer as of Feb. 1, 2027, succeeding Jamie Miller, who guided the company through a CEO transition. Bramley comes from Xero, a global small-business platform, where she served as CFO since April 2025. Before Xero, she served as CFO and Teradata and held senior finance roles at HP.

PayPal (PYPL) also named new heads for its Consumer Financial Services & Venmo and Payment Services & Crypto units, as well as a new executive to lead AI Business Transformation & Operations. Its chief risk officer, Aaron Webster, will leave the company. 

PayPal (PYPL) stock fell 2.8% in premarket trading.

Separately, the company said Brian J. Lee, Goldman Sachs' (GS) former chief risk officer, will join PayPal Holdings' (PYPL) board as of Nov. 30, 2026. Lee, with more than 30 years of experience in financial services, developed expertise in enterprise risk management, financial oversight, regulatory capital, and corporate governance.

"His financial acumen, understanding of complex global financial institutions, and commitment to strong governance will provide important perspective as we continue to advance PayPal's long-term strategy and deliver value for our shareholders," said PayPal (PYPL) Chair David Dorman.

As for other leadership changes, Kartik Mani will join PayPal (PYPL) as president and head of Consumer Financial Services & Venmo. He comes from American Express, where he currently serves as president of global network and partner services.

Suzan Kereere, who currently serves as PayPal's head of Global Markets, will become president and head of Payment Services & Crypto businesses. She succeeds Jeff Pomeroy, who has served as interim lead and will continue to manage Payment Services & Platform.

Juan Rio will join the company on Nov. 30, 2026, to become executive vice president of AI Business Transformation & Operations. He joins from Brightstar AI, where he serves as managing director and chief delivery officer.

Frank Keller will continue to lead Checkout Solutions & PayPal, including branded checkout.

Ratinder Bedi, senior vice president of Credit and Fraud Risk, will serve as interim head of the risk organization, while the company searches for a permanent successor to Webster.

data.title: Worldline restricted outflows, boosted inflows to lift cash flow before 2023 stock price crash - FT
data.description:
Worldline (WWLNF) (WRDLY) restricted outflows and boosted inflows before its financial result announcements in the years leading up to the 2023 share price crash, the Financial Times reported, citing documents and three people familiar with the company.

The company delayed payments to suppliers and sought cash advances from customers before half-yearly reporting dates, at least from 2021 to 2023, to lift its disclosed cash flow higher, according to the report published on Friday.

The French digital payments firm's share prices plunged in the fourth quarter of 2023, resulting in takeover speculations. Worldline had issued a shock profit warning in October 2023, which sent the stock prices lower. Credit Agricole (CRARF) was also said to be looking at ways to help out the company.

A PwC report published in late 2023 indicated that Worldline's profit-to-cash conversion rate would have been lower in 2021, 2022, and the first part of 2023 on a "fully normalized" basis, according to the FT.

data.title: PHINIA appoints Treasurer Gordon Muir as CFO
data.description:
PHINIA (PHIN) announced Friday the appointment of Gordon Muir as senior vice president and chief financial officer, effective January 1, 2027.

The company noted that Muir succeeds Chris Gropp, current SVP and CFO, who will retire, effective March 31, 2027.

Gropp will support the transition period starting January 1 through March 31, 2027, as Special Advisor, also reporting to Brady Ericson, president and chief executive officer, focusing on a smooth and well-coordinated transition of responsibilities.

The company noted that Gordon joined BorgWarner in 2007 and has been part of PHINIA since its spin-off in 2023. He currently serves as PHINIA's treasurer, with responsibility for treasury and investor relations, and has played a key role in the company's financial strategy and capital markets activities. 

Source: press release

data.title: Procter & Gamble plans to use AI and automation to free up cash
data.description:
Procter & Gamble (PG) is in the spotlight after the consumer products giant unveiled a renewed cost savings program during its Investor Day event on Thursday. Notably, the Cincinnati-based company committed to a total of another $10B in cost savings in four years through FY30, mostly focused on using AI capabilities to accelerate speed of execution to deliver higher consumer usage and solve consumer problems. A 20% to 30% reduction in product supply workforce (including contractors) and increased use of automation will also factor in.

Following the initiatives, Procter & Gamble (PG) plans to reinvest the extra savings in growth while assuming roughly flat headcount and media spending.

During a Q&A session, CFO Andre Schulten reiterated that the main focus is to reinvest in the business to create the volume and scale that leads to higher margins. "We think this is the right approach given the opportunity to tap in more value-conscious consumers who can then uptrade when disposable income improves," noted JPMorgan analyst Andrea Texeira on the update. "We came away confident that PG can count on its strong moats of digital capabilities, supply chain efficiency, and R&D leadership that should continue to reaccelerate the growth to tackle the remaining 21 out of 50 category/country combinations in which P&G needs to improve share," added Texiera. 

JPMorgan kept its Overweight rating on Procter & Gamble (PG) in place.

Shares of Procter & Gamble (PG) moved 1.3% higher in premarket trading to $169.98. The 52-week high is $173.59.
